title: CuteAFD core swap: K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core against its BF16 core (same experts) and against K4, in free generation and on fixed traces
question: On CuteAFD v4.0.0, is K4-Core-K6's longer thinking against K4 associated with its 6-bit core or with its routed experts?
engines: tpurtell/cuteafd v4.0.0 (coordinator image index sha256:e257bc61...), unmodified launcher
checkpoints: derived/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K4-Core-K6-BF16core @ 049c0180 (local derived checkpoint, built by prep/build_derived.py; not a producer release)
hardware: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (300 W); GPU only, experts local, no DGX Spark expert nodes

amendments: 2026-11-03T17:27:39-08:00: pre-flight unit check lists services only (chain-cs.sh); before any request

goals.question: Is the derived checkpoint (K4-Core-K6 with its 316 core tensors replaced by the BF16 originals) built correctly, and are its core bytes identical to K4's?
goals.added_source: protocol/PROTOCOL.md:23-27 (C-K6x core bytes = K4's; planner dry run)

design.instrument: build script, shard manifest and per-tensor hash comparison

goals.headline: 316 of 316 core tensors byte-identical to K4's; derived checkpoint 150,250 tensors (1,264 EXL3 core tensors removed, 316 BF16 added). CuteAFD's planner gives C-K6x the same plan as C-K4 except the MTP layer (dry-run logs, not published).

goals.question: Launch mechanics: pre-flight unit check lists services only.
goals.headline: First launch refused at pre-flight (a timer always 'active (waiting)'); chain-cs.sh's check limited to --type=service. No request sent, no data read; measures, arms, order and analysis unchanged.

goals.headline: Differences as K4-Core-K6's side minus the other. log p(</think>) at the close: core -0.011 [-0.039, +0.017], experts +0.004 [-0.025, +0.031], total -0.007 [-0.044, +0.026], not detected. Pre-close hazard not detected in any contrast; </think> top-1 at the close 0.909 in every arm. goals.headline: Post hoc. The max falls on the first scored row in 46 of 48 trace-arms (180 of 192 on the vLLM captures); question 13 (5 of 16 traces) carries the frozen max-p result (C-K4 1.49e-4 vs C-K6x 2.40e-5). With the opening row removed max p is about 1e-6 and the arm order changes from question to question.

goals.question: In free generation on code and prose, does the 6-bit core make K4-Core-K6 think longer than the same checkpoint with its BF16 core (core: C-K6 / C-K6x)?

design.instrument: free generation, v4 Block L stage L3 driver (cap 130,048, 2 concurrent, thinking on); reasoning tokens by re-tokenization with the frozen Block L analyzer
design.items: 8 Block L prompts (4 code, 4 prose), the same prompts and salt as Block L
design.repeats: 4 replies per prompt per arm (2 runs x 2 reps); 32 new seeds shared across arms, none from Block L r1/r2
design.interval: 95% bootstrap over the 8 prompts (primary) and the 32 pairs (secondary); ratio = exp(mean seed-paired log ratio); detected when the prompt interval excludes 1

goals.status_note: Followed on code by results/2026-11-05-code-thinking (12 new prompts; 1.26 [1.24, 1.29], detected). On the vLLM fork, where the two cores differ only in weight values, the same code prompts give 1.00 [0.96, 1.04] (2026-11-06-vllm-code-thinking), and on CuteAFD the BF16-core arm's code length moves with its KDA launch setting (2026-11-06-cuteafd-fp8-ablation, FA-kda-step). The CuteAFD 'core' contrast therefore also carries the launch settings that come with a BF16 core (FP8 KDA, head and prefill activations; VC-fp8-path).
goals.headline: Core C-K6 / C-K6x 1.16, prompt interval [0.98, 1.36]: not detected under the frozen primary rule; pair interval [1.01, 1.31] (secondary) excludes 1. By content: code 1.25, prose 1.08 (4 prompts each). CuteAFD v4.0.0; 'BF16 core' is BF16 converted to FP8 at load.
